title: FIRE DEPARTMENT GRANTS
full_story:
The Illinois Department of Natural Resources (IDNR) has awarded $495,000 in federal grants to 73 volunteer fire departments across the state to help with purchasing new equipment or paying for fire training.

The Volunteer Fire Capacity (VFC) grant program is funded by the U.S. Department of Agriculture Forest Service.  The program provides matching funds to aid fire departments in the purchase of new equipment and helps fund training.  Funding is passed through IDNR to local fire departments and fire training academies.

The 73 grantees provide fire protection to about 250,000 Illinois residents, primarily in rural areas of Illinois.  Locally the North Clay Fire Protection District, will receive $10,000, In Effingham County the Montrose Fire Protection District, will get $4,568, the Teutopolis Fire Protection District, gets $5,367.50, the Tri-County Fire Protection District, $9,958, and the Watson Fire Protection District, will receive $4,908.  In Wayne County the Fairfield Rural Fire Protection District, will get $9,480.50, and in Marion County the Salem Fire Protection District, will get $6,918.50.

The VFC grant program reimburses 50% of the recipients’ project costs up to $10,000.  Grant recipients must make the initial financial outlay for the projects before being reimbursed.

In 2025, the program awarded $322,893 for 48 Illinois projects.  The types of projects that have been funded under previous grants include radios, hoses, self-contained breathing apparatus, turn-out gear, wildland personal protective equipment, hand tools, chainsaws, backpack blowers, modifying federal excess vehicles and equipment, and other equipment.

title: BLOOD DRIVE
full_story:
The American Red Cross is asking you to donate blood as we head toward the summer months.  Blood donors are urgently needed because there has been a troubling drop in appointments which is putting pressure on the national blood supply.

There are two Blood Drives coming up this week.  The first is at the Blue Point Free Will Baptist Church tomorrow from Noon to 6 pm and the next is on Thursday, from Noon to 5 pm at the Flora Church of the Nazarene.  Donors at these drives will receive a $15 gift card by email.

Donors, especially those with type O blood and those giving platelets, can help bolster the blood supply now by making an appointment to give in the coming weeks.  Make an appointment to donate by downloading the free Red Cross Blood Donor App, visiting redcrossblood.org or calling 1-800-RED CROSS (1-800-733-2767).

title: PLUMMER ICASH EVENTS
full_story:
State Senator Jason Plummer is hosting an ICASH event in partnership with the Illinois State Treasurer’s Office.  Constituents are encouraged to stop by to check if they are owed unclaimed property and receive assistance filing a claim.

State Senator Jason Plummer said, “Too often, folks don’t realize they may have money or property waiting to be claimed.  These ICASH events make it easy for residents to stop by, get help from professionals, and find out if they have unclaimed property.  My goal is to make this service more convenient and ensure people get the assistance they need to reclaim what’s rightfully theirs.  The Treasurer’s Office has over $5 billion in unclaimed property owed to Illinois residents.”

The ICASH event will be at the Flora Volunteer Fire Department tomorrow from 10 am to 2 pm.

ICASH events help residents across Illinois locate and reclaim unclaimed property.  Since 2015, more than $2.5 billion in assets have been returned to Illinoisans.  Unclaimed property can include everything from forgotten bank accounts and uncashed checks to insurance payments, stocks, and even the contents of safe deposit boxes.

No reservations are required.  For more information, call Senator Plummer’s office at 618-283-3000.

title: CLAY COUNTY MOBILE HOME TAXES
full_story:
The 2026 Mobile Home Privilege Tax Bills were mailed out on Monday, April 20th.  The due date for mobile home taxes will be on July 1st, but you can pay the taxes at any time.  After July 1st, you will be charged an additional $25.00 per month.

If you did not receive a mobile home Privilege tax bill, and you own a mobile home, please contact the Treasurer’s office immediately at 618-665-3727 or email [email protected].  That will give the office time to investigate the matter before it is at risk of becoming delinquent.

Clay County taxpayers can pay their mobile home taxes by mail by sending their check with the payment stub to the Clay County Treasurer PO Box 88 Louisville 62858.  Mailed payments must be postmarked on or before the due date to avoid penalty.  Mobile home privilege tax bills can be paid at the Treasurer’s office in the Clay County Courthouse, they accept cash, check, cashier’s check, or money orders.  Please bring your entire bill if you want it stamped to show proof of payment.  The Clay County Treasurer’s office hours are from 8 am to 4 pm and they are open during the noon hour.  Payment can be made by placing payment in the envelope depository at the north entrance of the Clay County Courthouse.  Please include payment stub.  Tax Bills can also be paid online by credit/debit card by going to govpaynow.com PLC number a00082.

title: INTRODUCTION TO NURSING
full_story:
Lake Land College is hosting an Introduction to Nursing event for high school students on Tuesday, July 14th from 10 am to 4 pm in Neal Hall room 101.  The event is designed for students interested in the nursing profession to learn about the programs and resources available at Lake Land College as well as the career opportunities available in the field.

During the event, students in attendance will meet with faculty and staff, tour Lake Land’s nursing facilities and develop their skills in a variety of hands-on activities.  They will also enjoy the opportunity to experience and practice realistic patient care in the College’s high-fidelity patient simulation lab.  Additionally, attendees will learn everything they need to know about the nursing program admission process, from financial aid options to tips for the entrance exam.  A free pizza lunch will also be provided for all students in attendance.

Space for the Introduction to Nursing event is limited to the first 30 registrants.  Registration is available online.

The Lake Land College Introduction to Nursing Event is offered with sponsorship support from St. Anthony’s Memorial Hospital and Good Shepard Hospital.

To learn more about the Lake Land College Introduction to Nursing Event, contact Nursing Instructor Nichole Jones at 217-234-5455 or [email protected].

title: PLUMMER STATEMENT ON BEARS
full_story:
On Friday, the Chicago Bears organization announced it will advance its stadium development in Hammond, Indiana.  Upon learning the news, State Senator Jason Plummer issued the following statement:

“While I cannot say I am shocked by today’s announcement, I am extremely disappointed that Illinois has once again found itself on the losing end because of failed leadership in Springfield.

“The Chicago Bears moving forward with stadium development in Hammond, Indiana, is not just a sports story.  It is another warning sign that Illinois is losing jobs, investment, families, businesses, and now even one of its most iconic institutions because Governor Pritzker and his Democrat allies refuse to get serious about the direction of this state.

“This is what happens when state leaders are more focused on national political ambitions than fixing the problems right in front of them.  Illinois should be a place where people and businesses want to build, grow, and stay.  Under Governor Pritzker’s leadership, too many are looking for the exits.

“The Bears’ decision should be a wake-up call, but if history has shown us anything, it’s definitely that Pritzker doesn’t learn from his mistakes.”
